solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Ready to toy with carelessly, my one and only old mop

indicators.note: done carelessly, the letters are thrown together in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone casually fiddles with a cherished old mop, their one and only.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ready' is a noun here, slang for cash; 'and' just joins the fodder words.
explanation.definitionFit: Ready is slang for cash, and the banknotes in the board game are play cash to toy with.

clue.text: My twin girls, eg, excited about king character in Potter book

indicators.note: the mixed letters go about another letter
excited letters are stirred up into a new order

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: Twin girls are thrilled about a character in a Harry Potter story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Potter' suggests Harry, but it is Beatrix Potter, the children's author.
explanation.definitionFit: Mrs Tiggy-Winkle is the hedgehog washerwoman in a Beatrix Potter tale.

clue.text: Group that's got part of the joint jumping?

indicators.note: in a down answer the word jumps up, reading from bottom to top

parts.note: a tenon is the projecting piece of a mortise-and-tenon joint

explanation.surface: A band gets the bar jumping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joint' looks like a nightclub but is carpentry; 'jumping' turns TENON upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A nonet is a set of nine, especially nine musicians playing together.

clue.text: Man with fair promotion prospects given hand by Pole

parts.note: passed, as in passed the salt, means given
a paw is a hand, informally
N is the North Pole

explanation.surface: A worker with good career hopes gets help from a Polish colleague.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' is a chess piece and 'promotion' is a pawn reaching the last rank.
explanation.definitionFit: In chess a passed pawn has no enemy pawns blocking it, so it stands a fair chance of being promoted.

clue.text: Punch landed: so able to be seen by an old nurse?

definitions.text: able to be seen by an old nurse?

parts.note: lamp is British slang for punch or hit
a bird that has lit has landed

explanation.surface: A punch landed, so an elderly nurse could witness it.
explanation.walkthrough: The old nurse is Florence Nightingale, 'the Lady with the Lamp' of the Crimean War.
explanation.definitionFit: Anything lit by a lamp was visible to Nightingale on her night rounds.

clue.text: Grumble after collecting books in a state

indicators.note: the word collects the others inside it

parts.note: a moan is a grumble
NT is the New Testament, a set of books

explanation.surface: Someone moans after gathering their books while in a fluster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a state' sounds like agitation, but 'state' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Montana is one of the fifty United States.

clue.text: Victor leaves work, making time for a holiday

indicators.note: the letter leaves the word, taken out

parts.note: a novel is a literary work
Victor is V in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: Victor quits his job, freeing time to go on holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: Noel is Christmas, the festive season when most people take a break.

clue.text: Condemned a buyout, yet mostly getting expression of approval

indicators.note: condemned letters are knocked down and rebuilt in another order
mostly means the word loses its last letter

explanation.surface: Someone denounced a company buyout yet still got applause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims yet to YE before the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an Australian exclamation of delight or praise.

clue.text: Royal command following, popular with men fit for service

indicators.note: the royal command follows the rest

parts.note: in means popular or fashionable
OR, other ranks, means the men as opposed to officers
a king is royal
an order is a command

explanation.surface: A king's decree follows, popular with soldiers declared fit to serve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'men' gives OR, other ranks in the army.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine in working order functions properly, so it is serviceable.

clue.text: Channel, small, across the pond

parts.note: S is the usual abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
seen from Britain, across the Atlantic is in the US

explanation.surface: A small waterway lies over on the far side of the Atlantic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Across the pond' is British idiom for America, so it gives IN US.
explanation.definitionFit: A sinus is a cavity or passage in the body, such as the nasal channels.

clue.text: Model, short type, with one child of five

indicators.note: short means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a manner is a kind or type, as in 'all manner of'
a quin is one of quintuplets

explanation.surface: A model is described as a short type who is a quintuplet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short type' looks like a person's height but it means a word for 'type' cut short.
explanation.definitionFit: A mannequin is a dummy, or a person, used to display clothes, i.e. a fashion model.

clue.text: Where there are no trees, having abandoned home — good being out of the woods!

indicators.note: abandoning something means dropping it from the phrase
'good being out' reads as the letter for good being removed, with 'out' shared with the definition

parts.note: a clearing is open ground in a wood, so a place without trees is in the clearing
IN means at home

explanation.surface: Escaping the forest and leaving home behind feels like being safe at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having abandoned' drops IN and 'being (out)' drops G, removing the final ING of the phrase; 'out' serves both the deletion and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases are idioms for being free of danger or difficulty.

clue.text: Visiting Europe, sought change from S America

indicators.note: the answer pays a visit inside these words, sitting within them

explanation.surface: A traveller in Europe goes looking for South American currency.
explanation.definitionFit: The peso is the currency, and so the coins and small change, of several South American countries.

clue.text: Rely on crab moving a fraction of an inch

indicators.note: moving the letters around gives a new order

explanation.surface: Trust a crab to scuttle a tiny distance.
explanation.definitionFit: The barleycorn was an old unit of length, a third of an inch, from a grain's size.

clue.text: Degenerate acquired drug to carry round

indicators.note: the two words carry the letter between them

parts.note: got means acquired
pot is slang for cannabis
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A degenerate gets hold of some drugs to take around with them.
explanation.definitionFit: To go to pot is an idiom for falling into decline or ruin, i.e. to deteriorate.

clue.text: Don't report everything subject to discrimination

definitions.meaning: to ... is to report only a portion

explanation.surface: Advice to keep quiet about prejudice one has suffered.
explanation.definitionFit: Telling things apart means distinguishing between them, which is discrimination in the neutral sense.

clue.text: Cheers to the left and right in this country for old statesman

indicators.note: in an across answer, going to the left means read backwards

parts.note: ta-ta and cheers are both informal British farewells

indicators.note: the letter goes in the country's abbreviation

parts.note: for a British newspaper, this country is the UK

explanation.surface: Cheering on both sides greets a former leader of this nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cheers' means goodbye here, not applause; a London paper's 'this country' is Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Kemal Atatürk was the founding president of modern Turkey, a statesman of the last century.

clue.text: Source, I heard, honestly come by

parts.note: a well is a source of water

indicators.note: heard means the word is replaced by one sounding the same

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone claims they heard their source came by something honestly.
explanation.walkthrough: I stands for one, said the same as WON.
explanation.definitionFit: A victory gained fairly and deservedly is called well-won.

clue.text: One recently arrived dined under gaslight

indicators.note: in a down answer, under means placed after

parts.note: neon is a gas used in lighting
ate means dined

explanation.surface: A newcomer ate a meal beneath a gas lamp.
explanation.definitionFit: A neonate is a newborn baby, a very recent arrival in the world.

clue.text: Asian island, a place tucked away

indicators.note: the letters are tucked away inside the island's name

parts.note: the Isle of Man is a crossword favourite island
to lay something is to place it

explanation.surface: An Asian island has a spot hidden somewhere on it.
explanation.definitionFit: Malayan describes a person or thing from Malaya, in Southeast Asia.

clue.text: Halfway through Hilary maybe tried crudely interrupting Mark and Mike

indicators.note: the mixed letters break into the space between the others

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for mark, the old German currency
Mike is M in the NATO alphabet

indicators.note: crudely done, the letters are roughly rearranged

explanation.surface: Hilary crudely attempted to cut in on two men, Mark and Mike.
explanation.walkthrough: Hilary is not a person but the Oxford University spring term.
explanation.definitionFit: Midterm is the middle point of an academic term, of which Hilary is an example.

clue.text: Failure to see case for amateurish boat-builder

parts.note: 'no' is a refusal, a failure to see someone's point or agree

indicators.note: a case encloses, so the word's outer letters

explanation.surface: An amateur boat-builder lacks vision and so needs a case made.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case for' takes the outside letters of 'amateurish'.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis Noah built the ark, making him the Bible's best-known shipwright.

clue.text: Fix that's welcome?

definitions.meaning: a fine ... is a muddle or predicament, a fix
the phrase is a formal greeting on meeting someone

explanation.surface: A puzzled host asks whether some repair counts as welcome.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is both a polite greeting and, in 'a fine how-do-you-do', an awkward mess.

clue.text: Every so often, turns head to uncover it

indicators.note: every so often picks out every other letter of the words

explanation.surface: From time to time someone turns their head to reveal it.
explanation.walkthrough: The even letters are taken; 'it' points at the head that is bared.
explanation.definitionFit: To uncover can mean to bare one's head as a courtesy, removing one's hat.

clue.text: Blessed fellow dated you — a sore point!

parts.note: ST is short for saint, a blessed person
ye is an old form of you

explanation.surface: A saintly man went out with you, a painful matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dated' looks like romance but means old-fashioned.
explanation.definitionFit: A stye is a painful swelling on the eyelid, literally a sore spot.

clue.text: People after area in abandoned section of plant

indicators.note: the people's word comes after the rest
the letter goes in the other word

parts.note: something abandoned is left
a race is a people

explanation.surface: People turn up after a region of some deserted part of a factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plant' could be a factory; here it is botanical.
explanation.definitionFit: A leaf trace is the strand of vascular tissue running from a stem into a leaf, a part of the plant.

clue.text: Sounded thrilled to have escaped, gradually having change of heart

indicators.note: the middle letter of the word is swapped for another

parts.note: liquid that has oozed has seeped out slowly

explanation.surface: Someone who slowly got away later had second thoughts but was delighted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change of heart' swaps the central Z for H.
explanation.definitionFit: To ooh is to utter a sound of delight or wonder.

clue.text: Picture tango, with fellow getting closer

parts.note: Tango is T in the NATO alphabet
he is a fellow, a male person
a terminator is something that closes or ends things

explanation.surface: A tango dancer gets closer to a fellow in a photograph.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Picture' means a film, the 1984 Schwarzenegger science-fiction movie.
explanation.definitionFit: A picture is a film, and this is a famous action film.
